subject: Renewal pricing concession and commit re-anchor
messages:
From: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@hummingcode.com>
Date: 2026-09-06T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal pricing concession and commit re-anchor

Hi Aisha,

We’re coming up on your Aug 31 contract anniversary and I wanted to get ahead of the renewal discussion so we don’t impact your spike planning for Q4. Quick summary of what I’m proposing so your team can evaluate it with procurement: 

- 6-month price hold at current blended rate if Hummingcode signs the attached 12-month committed term by Sept 30.
- Modest stepped discount (5% year 1 -> 3% year 2) in exchange for a firm minimum-commit baseline (re-anchor) that reflects your projected 20% YoY growth.
- One-time operational credit of $18,000 to offset migration of three heavy pipelines to our dedicated pool (applies on invoice after go-live).
- Scale-on-demand burst buffer: additional 20% burst headroom billed at a discounted overage rate.

I’ve attached a comparison workbook with the current baseline, the proposed commit re-anchor, and a short P&L view showing net unit cost. If this aligns with what you need, I’ll loop in Karthik and Marissa to handle commercial redlines and onboarding dates. If procurement needs a more conservative alternative, I can provide a 9-month price hold variant instead.

Next steps I’d recommend: procurement review + a 30-min call this week to agree final commit and PO timing. Are you available Thu or Fri?

Thanks,
Lukas
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Hummingcode_Pricing_Option_A_v2.xlsx]

From: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@hummingcode.com>
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir.patel@hummingcode.com>
Date: 2026-09-07T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal pricing concession and commit re-anchor

Thanks Lukas — appreciate the early heads up. High level response from procurement and finance: 

- Price hold is helpful, but procurement is asking for the hold to cover Q4 planning (need it thru 2027-03-31). Would you consider extending the protected window to 6 months plus the remainder of Q4 (effectively ~9 months) if we sign by Sept 30?
- The one-time operational credit looks reasonable; finance will ask for that to be clearly itemized on the PO.
- We need more detail on burst pricing (can you provide exact per-token or per-request rates for the discounted overage tier?).

Samir (copied) will handle the detailed numbers — he’ll take the workbook and come back with a counter by Wednesday. I’m also copying legal (legal@hummingcode.com) to fast-track the redlines.

Can you hold Thursday 3pm PT for a working session? If yes, we’ll confirm and send a short agenda.

Best,
Aisha
Director, Cloud Procurement | Hummingcode Systems

From: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@hummingcode.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@hummingcode.com>, legal@hummingcode.com
Date: 2026-09-07T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal pricing concession and commit re-anchor

Aisha / Samir — great, thanks for the quick reply. Thursday 3pm PT works for us — I’ll send a calendar invite after this note. A few clarifications ahead of the call so procurement has numbers to review: 

- Extended hold option: we can do a 9-month protected window that ends 2027-03-31 as you requested, with the same economics as the 6-month hold but a slightly larger operational credit ($22,000) to compensate for the longer lock. I modeled both options in the attached sheet (Option A = 6-month hold + $18k credit, Option B = 9-month hold + $22k credit).
- Burst pricing: discounted overage tier = $0.0045 /k tokens processed (applies to dedicated pool bursts beyond baseline). I’ve added a worked example for your 3 biggest pipelines to show estimated monthly overage under several scenarios.
- Commit re-anchor mechanics: baseline is an annual committed token floor. True-ups quarterly; unused committed units can be banked for 60 days. We included a small stepdown clause in year 2 to protect against early churn (detailed in workbook).

Attachments included in this message: Hummingcode_Pricing_Option_A_v2.xlsx (two tabs: Option A and Option B) and a draft terms sheet. Karthik — can you confirm whether our legal team is comfortable with the 60-day bank window and the burst discount language? Marissa — can your CS ops team validate the migration timeline (we proposed a 6-week plan in the workbook).

Attachment: [Hummingcode_Pricing_Option_A_v2.xlsx]

Thanks,
Lukas
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Hummingcode Legal <legal@hummingcode.com>
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-09T16:48:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal pricing concession and commit re-anchor — redline

Lukas — attaching a redline to the draft terms. Legal is generally comfortable with the 9-month hold + $22k credit (Option B) provided three small edits are made: 

1) Add explicit language that the operational credit will be applied as a separate line item on the first invoice post go-live and is not refundable.
2) Clarify that burst overage charges are capped at 2x the discounted overage rate for any single billing month if usage exceeds 3x baseline (protects us from runaway cost in a spike month).
3) Replace the 60-day bank window with a 90-day bank window; finance prefers the longer carryover to smooth true-ups.

We’re happy to sign Option B with those edits. Please confirm and send a final doc + PO instructions and we’ll get the signature process started.

[Attachment: Hummingcode_Renewal_Term_Draft_Redline.pdf]

Regards,
Hummingcode Legal Team
legal@hummingcode.com
